BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. The Seller documents are treated as untrusted counterparty material.

## Preliminary points

1. **Two Seller positions match our fallbacks, but neither is authorised.** The 20% cap and the 18-month claims period both equal playbook fallbacks. Neither fallback can be used without Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given. The Seller calls its positions "key negotiated positions", "agreed price mechanics", "fair and balanced", "adequate" and "settled". None of these labels has been confirmed through our authority process, so they carry no weight.
2. **The Disclosure Letter facts are dated 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago.** We should refresh the facts on Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-006, Ironquay and Sandbar before relying on them. We should also keep verified updates separate from Seller assertions.
3. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts parts of its Update.** For example, the Update says "Bluefen consent is addressed", but Disclosure Letter item 2 says there is no final consent and no evidence of conditions. We should use these admissions in the mark-up.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000), cl 12.1.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter at AUD 6,000,000.
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft, which we do not have.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis. AUD 250,000 basket, recoverable only above the basket (deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 5,000 de minimis. AUD 50,000 basket, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping.
- **Reason:** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and the deductible structure permanently removes the first AUD 250,000 of loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3/13). Any limitation also applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims, with separate periods for other categories.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the 18 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" language.
- **Reason:** 18 months is an unapproved fallback, and the blanket wording would cut Title, Tax, indemnity and fraud periods.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties fall under the general caps and time limits, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Title and capacity go to the root of what we are buying, and simplicity is no reason to cap them at 20%.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Insert an express carve-out.
- **Reason:** The "any nature" wording would purport to shelter fraud. This is non-negotiable, and no one may waive it.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Delete DL 1.1–1.2 and any deemed-disclosure language.
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure moves the diligence risk back to us and empties the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything known to the Buyer or its advisers, or discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier must use named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Delete cl 8.3.
- **Reason:** It is a blanket exclusion based on imputed knowledge that could defeat even the specific indemnities.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Addressed". Reasonable endeavours only, and the condition is satisfied on delivery of the written consent (cl 3/6.3).
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent, plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Completion condition.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m). DL item 2 admits there is no final consent and no condition evidence, so "addressed" is inaccurate.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion" for about AUD 3,200,000 (cl 2/7).
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** DL item 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and undischarged. A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and similar) as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require an express line item, with on-costs quantified.
- **Reason:** DL item 5 admits the amounts are not in the funds flow and that on-costs are unaddressed. The Company would bear a silent liability after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader IP indemnity covering ownership, infringement and transfer of the Project Materials. The SOW3 cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment) should be preserved.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow form and broaden it. Request proof of payment, or require cure before Completion.
- **Reason:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer depends on payment of every SOW3 fee, and no receipt or assignment exists. The AUD 180,000 figure in DD-010 is not independently verified either way, so the indemnity should not be pinned to it.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, an ongoing investigation, regular updates to the Buyer, and appropriate warranty or indemnity protection.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the immateriality characterisation. Require covenants to preserve, investigate and update.
- **Reason:** About 1,240 records may be affected and scope is unknown. However, there is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure, so we should neither accept the Seller's reassurance nor assert a breach or numeric demand ourselves. Refresh the status, which is dated 22 September.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course, and how they relate in timing and scope (DD-008/DD-011).
- **Recommendation:** Reserve the position pending diligence. Do not concede ordinary course, and do not claim automatic Debt treatment or a price deduction.
- **Reason:** DL item 8 states none of these facts, so neither side's classification is established yet.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature". Any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise". Tax/IP fall under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment-obligation and covenant categories kept separate, each with its own regime, and no general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Insert express carve-outs and an order-of-precedence clause.
- **Reason:** These are hidden overrides that would collapse every protection into the 20% / 18-month general regime.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority, such as ASIC extract, PPSR search, constitution, board approvals and share certificates. Title warranties should sit in the fundamental regime.
- **Recommendation:** Not accepted as sufficient.
- **Reason:** DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller. DL item 10 itself concedes it is not Buyer verification.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** These terms treated as OPEN, to be negotiated as separate categories.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" assertion and keep them open.
- **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed through our authority process. We are not assuming unlimited liability or any resolution, but they must not default into the general cap.

---

## Escalation and next steps
- **No authority to concede:** No fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) may be offered unless Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying this draft.
- **Information requests to the Seller:**
  - Updated Bluefen consent and evidence of the cl 11.3 conditions.
  - Riverlark payout letter and draft releases.
  - Bonus on-cost calculations.
  - Ironquay payment evidence.
  - DD-006 investigation update and log-preservation confirmation.
  - Sandbar contract terms.
  - Independent title searches.
- **Mark-up priorities:** Fraud carve-out (SPA-N-005), the category and override language (SPA-N-003, 004, 014), and the Completion conditions (SPA-N-008, 009, 010).
